How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Bit difficult - if you want something affordable and not an old brothel turned student housing.
The place I lived was fine - Student Republic was the name, Tesla Apartments. 
The cheapest I could find (while still loking legit).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living in Old Town is not necessarily fun - loads of people all the time. There are some pretty nice areas just outside city centre. It's just expensive living in Prague.
Our landlords did us dirty the first month; we had recieved two account numbers for payment - a czech and a eur acc. However the only one we got an IBAN number for was the EUR one, and if we wanted to use that one, we had to use their own conversion rate - which made our rent 500dkk higher. So we paid that the first month since it wasn't possible for us to use the czech acc and pay in czk. But then after three passive aggressive emails they sent us the IBAN for the czech account. 
Don't fall into that trap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There's a list provided on the uni website with available ersamus courses for each faculty - however, when you go to the registration system, SIS, some look a bit different and some are just not available. It was difficult to make a realistic schedule since each course was 1-5 points which means you need a lot of courses to reach 30.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The lady at the erasmus office was nice, but mostly advised me to write to the teachers for each course if I had questions or wasn't sure whether or not I could enroll.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat. I didn't get half the courses I initially had approved from home since they had reached capacity, were cancelled or not available in english. But the ones I got were still (mostly) relevant and interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a lot of courses pre-approved - makes it so much easier to create a schedule where the lectures don't overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mostly MA since they were in english.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Soewhat the same. More rote learning though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Landscape Changes and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Forest Geography
Field exercises in Botany
Field Course in Restoration Ecology
Ecology in landscape and urban design

The excursion courses were really fun and rewarding.
Forest Geography gave a broader sense of climate and ecosystems than I had before.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
You had to pay for excursions, which is not mentioned until well into the semester.
Going out almost always came with expences.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and groceries more expensive, eating out cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Loads of trips to other cities and countries. Pub crawls and quizzes

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The trips outside Prague were fun and cheap.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out of Prague and see the countryside and forests. Hiking and cycling.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, since it's pretty similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It doesn't necessarily come naturally, so you have to actively try.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You had to be overly polite to elderly people in order to avoid getting slagged off. Had a guy ~70 repeatedly bump his supermarket cart into me in the queue since I apparantly wasn't moving fast enough. Also there's a tendency amongst the elderly part of the population the be a bit xenophobic :(

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sense of heritage. Lots of beautiful churches, streets and castles.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take advantage of the cheap transport.
Stay away from Duplex
Go on field trips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some teachers don't have high expectations when it comes to exchange students, but some do, and it IS possible to fail an exam. (Especially since usually only the teacher is present at exams)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting loads of new people and seeing my studies from a different perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Budgetting and keeping up with social stuff while actually studying.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
